# OAuth broker

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P3 · Act as the user](../README.md#phase-3--act-as-the-user) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:oauth-broker` · **Epic:** [#132](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/132) · **Tickets:** 5 (2S 3M)

The CP brokers OAuth authorization code + PKCE flows to third-party providers on behalf of signed-in employees, starting with Google and GitHub. Tokens go straight to the secret backend at warden/users/<sub>/<provider>; the CP keeps only grant metadata.

## How we build it

- Provider config (consent.providers[]): id, type (google|github|generic), clientID, clientSecretRef (secret store key or env var), authURL, tokenURL, revokeURL, allowedScopes[], extraAuthParams (e.g. access_type=offline, prompt=consent for Google). Built-in defaults per type; generic requires all URLs.
- Flow: GET /connect/start?provider=&scopes=&pending= (portal session required) creates pending_authorizations(id, sub, provider, scopes, state_hash, pkce_verifier_ref, agent_id, status, created_at, expires_at 15m) and redirects; GET /connect/callback validates state against the current portal session's sub and the pending id, exchanges code with PKCE verifier, writes tokens, marks pending granted.
- Scope capping: requested scopes = intersection of request, provider allowedScopes and the agent's per-user secret mapping scopes from policy; scopes outside the cap return 400 before any redirect.
- Token write: JSON {refresh_token, access_token, expiry, scope, token_type} via SecretStore.Put to warden/users/<sub>/<provider>; grants table grants(sub, provider, scopes, granted_at, updated_at, last_used_at, revoked_at) has no value column.
- GitHub OAuth apps issue non-expiring tokens without refresh: store access_token with expiry=0; GitHub Apps user tokens with refresh are supported when the provider returns refresh_token.

## Done when

A signed-in employee can connect Google and GitHub, the tokens land in the secret backend under warden/users/<sub>/<provider>, and the CP database holds only grant metadata.

### 1/5 · W-P3-BRKR-01

**Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#133](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/133)

New package internal/oauthbroker with type Provider {ID, Type, ClientID, ClientSecretRef, AuthURL, TokenURL, RevokeURL, AllowedScopes, ExtraAuthParams} and a Registry built from consent.providers in internal/config. Fill defaults for type google (accounts.google.com auth, oauth2.googleapis.com token and revoke, access_type=offline, prompt=consent) and github (github.com/login/oauth/authorize and access_token; revoke via DELETE /applications/{client_id}/grant). Client secrets resolve through the SecretStore or env at startup and are never logged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A google provider with only clientID and clientSecretRef resolves full URLs
- [ ] A generic provider missing tokenURL fails config validation
- [ ] Unknown provider ids are rejected by Registry.Get

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-CSIG-01`](consent-auth.md#14--w-p3-csig-01) Add consent.oidc config block and portal OIDC client

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-02`](oauth-broker.md#25--w-p3-brkr-02) Add pending authorization and grant metadata stores; [`W-P3-BRKR-05`](oauth-broker.md#55--w-p3-brkr-05) Add provider revoke client for Google and GitHub

### 2/5 · W-P3-BRKR-02

**Add pending authorization and grant metadata stores**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#134](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/134)

Add CP SQLite migrations for pending_authorizations and grants (columns as in the item design) behind a GrantStore interface in internal/oauthbroker so Postgres can replace it later. Methods: CreatePending, GetPending, CompletePending(id, status), ExpirePending (run from the CP retention ticker), UpsertGrant, ListGrants(sub), RevokeGrant(sub, provider), TouchLastUsed(sub, provider, agent). State is stored as SHA-256; the PKCE verifier is held in the pending row encrypted with a CP-local key, never logged.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Pending rows past expires_at move to status=expired on the next prune
- [ ] UpsertGrant twice for the same (sub, provider) leaves one row with updated_at advanced
- [ ] A reflect test asserts grants has no value-bearing field

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#15--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-03`](oauth-broker.md#35--w-p3-brkr-03) Implement /connect/start with PKCE and agent scope capping; [`W-P3-JIT-01`](jit-authorization.md#15--w-p3-jit-01) Add CP endpoint to create or reuse pending authorizations

### 3/5 · W-P3-BRKR-03

**Implement /connect/start with PKCE and agent scope capping**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#135](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/135)

Add GET /connect/start?provider=&scopes=&pending= in internal/oauthbroker, mounted on the CP and wrapped by the portal session middleware (unauthenticated users go to /portal/login and return). Compute capped scopes = requested ∩ provider.AllowedScopes ∩ the agent mapping scopes for the pending's agent_id from the current policy; reject with 400 if any requested scope is outside the cap. Create or reuse the pending row bound to the session's sub, generate state and PKCE S256, and redirect to the provider authURL.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Redirect URL carries code_challenge_method=S256, state and only capped scopes
- [ ] Requesting a scope not in allowedScopes returns 400 with no pending row created
- [ ] A pending id belonging to a different sub returns 403

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-02`](oauth-broker.md#25--w-p3-brkr-02) Add pending authorization and grant metadata stores; [`W-P3-CSIG-04`](consent-auth.md#44--w-p3-csig-04) Add CSRF protection and session isolation from console

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-BRKR-04`](oauth-broker.md#45--w-p3-brkr-04) Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to secret backend; [`W-P3-PORT-03`](consent-portal.md#34--w-p3-port-03) Add pending authorization landing page

### 4/5 · W-P3-BRKR-04

**Implement /connect/callback and write tokens to secret backend**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#136](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/136)

Add GET /connect/callback: look up pending by state hash, require the current portal session sub to match, exchange code + verifier at tokenURL, write the token JSON via SecretStore.Put to warden/users/<sub>/<provider>, UpsertGrant with granted scopes as returned by the provider, mark pending granted and wake status waiters (W-P3-JIT-04). Provider errors (access_denied, invalid_grant) mark the pending denied and render an error page. Emit an admin audit event connect.granted with sub, provider, scopes and the secret Reference.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Against a fake provider in test/fakes, the secret store holds the token JSON and grants has one row
- [ ] A callback with a valid state but a different session sub returns 403 and writes nothing
- [ ] access_denied from the provider sets pending status=denied
- [ ] No log line contains the access or refresh token

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-03`](oauth-broker.md#35--w-p3-brkr-03) Implement /connect/start with PKCE and agent scope capping

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-PORT-01`](consent-portal.md#14--w-p3-port-01) Serve portal page and grants list API

### 5/5 · W-P3-BRKR-05

**Add provider revoke client for Google and GitHub**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#137](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/137)

Add oauthbroker.Revoke(ctx, provider, tokenJSON) that calls Google's revoke endpoint with the refresh token (falling back to access token) and GitHub's DELETE /applications/{client_id}/grant with basic auth. Treat 200 and provider not-found/invalid_token as success; return a typed error for retryable failures. Used by the portal revoke and offboarding.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Fake Google revoke receives the refresh token form-encoded
- [ ] Fake GitHub revoke receives DELETE with client basic auth and the access_token body
- [ ] An already-revoked token is reported as success

**Depends on:** [`W-P3-BRKR-01`](oauth-broker.md#15--w-p3-brkr-01) Add provider config model with Google and GitHub defaults

**Unblocks:** [`W-P3-PORT-02`](consent-portal.md#24--w-p3-port-02) Implement revoke: provider revoke, vault delete, worker invalidation
